newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - DEC 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - DEC 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The South African government's "Jobs for South Africa" project, in terms of which 11,000 affirmative action posts were advertised in the public service, has been abandoned with fewer than a quarter of the positions filled.

- Water Affairs and Forestry Minister Kader Asmal has allowed talks on the possible sale of state-owned South African Forestry Co (Safcol) to continue and restructuring options are being investigated with a decision likely next year.

- Printing and publishing group Caxton Ltd will take legal action next year to close all Independent Newspaper Ltd's magazines and free distribution newspapers nationwide, severely limiting the group's growth prospects.
- The cost of local telephone calls is to rise 28.4 percent as part of telecommunications parastatal Telkom's tariff restructuring plan and move to a more open market.

- Plummeting television sales predictions and declining tariff protection have thrown the one billion rand a year local television assembly industry into uncertainty, forcing some assemblers to retrench workers, cut back on production or shelve further expansion plans, industry sources said.

- Telkom's planned tariff increases, due to come into effect in the new year, will probably raise telephone costs for South African businesses by less than the inflation rate in the year ahead, according to Brian Clark, Telkom's managing director and chief executive.
- South Africa's debilitating "brain drain" took a breather in September, according to the latest monthly immigration and emigration figures released by the Central Statistical Service.
- AIG , the US-based international insurance group, lauched a joint venture with the South African National Civics Organisation to sell consumer insurance products in South Africa.
- Telkom will charge 28 percent more for local phone calls from next month -- an increase of six cents for every three minutes.
- The government has scrapped its programme aimed at filling 11,000 affirmative action civil service positions, Public Service Administration Minister Zola Skweyiya announced.

- The release of convicted killer policeman Brian Mitchell this week has raised the amnesty hopes of Clive Derby-Lewis and Janusz Walus, convicted killers of South African Communist Party leader Chris Hani.
